declarations.description:
A pure positional seam (root README's "positional seams" category) —
always present, giving a theme a stable, addressable box for the
button's text content instead of an anonymous projected text node no
stylesheet can reach. Carries no state of its own and consumes none:
unlike Checkbox's indicators, nothing about a label's presence or
appearance depends on hwc-button's state — it's a direct child by
construction (GUIDELINES.md rule 4's carve-out). Disabled dimming
reaches it for free through ordinary CSS inheritance of `color`, since
hwc-button's own disabled state-to-token mapping sets `color` on itself
rather than a property this element would need to independently mirror.

Not self-registering — call ButtonLabel.define() (optionally with a tag
name of your own choosing) before use. See GUIDELINES.md rule 5.
declarations.name: ButtonLabel

declarations.description: A pure positional seam (root README's "positional seams" category) — present only when the consumer projects one, giving a theme a fixed, addressable box to size and center regardless of what's projected (an SVG, an ``, a glyph). Carries no state and consumes none: it's a direct child by construction (GUIDELINES.md rule 4's carve-out), and disabled dimming reaches a `currentColor`-based icon for free through ordinary CSS inheritance from hwc-button's own `color`. Not self-registering — call ButtonLeadingIcon.define() (optionally with a tag name of your own choosing) before use. See GUIDELINES.md rule 5.
declarations.name: ButtonLeadingIcon

slots.description: The consumer's own icon (an SVG, an ``, anything).

declarations.description:
Headless button root — state, behavior, and accessibility only.
See button/SPEC.md for the composition contract and GUIDELINES.md for
why there's no native `<button>` underneath.

A pure form *operator* (GUIDELINES.md rule 8, category 2), not a
value-bearing control: formAssociated exists solely to acquire
internals.form — setFormValue() is never called, so hwc-button never
appears in FormData under any name. On activation, type="submit" calls
internals.form?.requestSubmit() (never submit(), so the submit event
fires and validation runs) and type="reset" calls internals.form?.reset();
type="button" (the default — a deliberate divergence from native's
submit-by-default) touches the form not at all. Fieldset disable arrives
through formDisabledCallback, OR'd with the consumer's own disabled
attribute exactly like Checkbox/Radio.

Not self-registering — call Button.define() (optionally with a tag name
of your own choosing) before use. See GUIDELINES.md rule 5.
declarations.name: Button

declarations.description:
A pure slot — the projected content owns the actual mark's shape; this
element only owns filling/centering itself in its parent box and mapping
its own state to design tokens (GUIDELINES.md rule 3), both of which are
tag-name-agnostic via :host and so survive a consumer renaming the tag.

Consumes hwc-checkbox's state over context and mirrors it into custom
states on its own ElementInternals — never as attributes, so the light
DOM stays entirely the consumer's (GUIDELINES.md rule 4). Not
self-registering — call CheckboxCheckedIndicator.define() (optionally
with a tag name of your own choosing) before use. See GUIDELINES.md rule 5.
declarations.name: CheckboxCheckedIndicator

slots.description: The consumer's own check mark (an SVG, a glyph, anything).

declarations.name: checkboxContext
declarations.description:
Broadcasts hwc-checkbox's state to its indicator children so each one can
decide its own visibility. Nothing here identifies a descendant by tag
name — see GUIDELINES.md rules 4 and 5 for why that matters once tag
names are consumer-configurable.

tag-name-agnostic via :host and so survive a consumer renaming the tag.

Consumes hwc-checkbox's state over context and mirrors it into custom
states on its own ElementInternals — never as attributes, so the light

declarations.name: CheckboxIndeterminateIndicator

slots.description: The consumer's own indeterminate mark (an SVG, a glyph, anything).

declarations.description:
Headless checkbox root — state, behavior, and accessibility only.
See checkbox/SPEC.md for the composition contract and GUIDELINES.md
for why there's no native `<input type="checkbox">` underneath.

Form-associated (GUIDELINES.md rule 8): submits `value` under `name`
while checked and nothing while unchecked, honors form.reset() and
`<fieldset disabled>`, and restores state on session restore — all
through the same ElementInternals handle the context indicators use.
Outside a form every one of those is a silent no-op.

Not self-registering — call Checkbox.define() (optionally with a tag
name of your own choosing) before use. See GUIDELINES.md rule 5.
declarations.name: Checkbox

events.name: change
events.description: Dispatched after checked/indeterminate changes from a click or Space keypress.

declarations.description:
The field's description part — a pure slot for secondary text (format
hints, consequences, helper text). Joins the claimed control's
aria-describedby through the field root, and dims itself while that
control is disabled, via a custom state consumed over the field context
(GUIDELINES.md rule 4).

Not self-registering — call FieldDescription.define() (optionally with
a tag name of your own choosing) before use. See GUIDELINES.md rule 5.
declarations.name: FieldDescription

slots.description: The description text for the field's control.

declarations.description:
The field's error-message part — state-mounted: renders only while the
field root's `error` is set, hidden until context proves otherwise, the
same custom-state visibility mechanism as Checkbox's indicators
(GUIDELINES.md rules 3 and 4). Deliberately no live region — no
role="alert" — announcement timing is validation policy, which belongs
to the application; a consumer who wants immediate announcement puts
role="alert" on the content they project (see field/SPEC.md).

Not self-registering — call FieldError.define() (optionally with a tag
name of your own choosing) before use. See GUIDELINES.md rule 5.
declarations.name: FieldError

slots.description: The validation message shown while the field is in error.

declarations.description:
The field's label part — a pure slot the consumer projects the label
text into. Not focusable, no role: it's text. Owns label activation —
clicking it focuses and clicks the field's claimed control, native
`<label>` parity, inert while that control is disabled — and dims itself
while the control is disabled via a custom state consumed over the
field context (GUIDELINES.md rule 4). Registration, id self-management,
and the disabled state come from FieldPart.

Not self-registering — call FieldLabel.define() (optionally with a tag
name of your own choosing) before use. See GUIDELINES.md rule 5.
declarations.name: FieldLabel

slots.description: The label text naming the field's control.

declarations.description:
Shared behavior of the three field text parts (label, description,
error) — not itself a custom element. Each part registers itself with
the nearest field root over context (never discovered by tag name —
GUIDELINES.md rule 5), assigns itself an id for the IDREF wiring if the
consumer didn't (the same self-managed-host-attribute pattern as a
control setting its own role and tabindex), and mirrors the context's
claimed-control state into custom states on its own ElementInternals
for styling (GUIDELINES.md rule 4).
declarations.name: FieldPart

declarations.description:
Headless field root — the shared label/description/error wrapper every
labeled control composes with. Owns no widget behavior; its job is
association, run entirely over context (field-context.ts): parts
register themselves, and the first field-aware control to claim gets
the parts wired to it — never discovered by tag name (GUIDELINES.md
rules 4 and 5). See field/SPEC.md for the full contract.

Not self-registering — call Field.define() (optionally with a tag name
of your own choosing) before use. See GUIDELINES.md rule 5.
declarations.name: Field

slots.description: The field's parts and its one control, in any order.

declarations.name: defineOnce
declarations.description:
Registers `ctor` under `tagName` unless that name is already taken, or
`ctor` was already registered under a different name — the native
registry throws if the same constructor is defined twice under any name,
so a repeat call (e.g. two entry points importing the same component)
must be a safe no-op, not a crash. See GUIDELINES.md rule 5.

The entire control side of the field contract (field/SPEC.md), shared
by every field-aware control — a component opts in with a single line:

  private _fieldClaim = new FieldClaimController(this, () => this._effectiveDisabled);

The controller claims the nearest field on connect (first claimant
wins — and it retries whenever a broadcast shows the seat empty, so a
removed claimant's seat passes to whoever remains), writes
aria-labelledby/aria-describedby IDREFs on the host from the field's
delivered parts, reports the host's effective disabled back so the text
parts can dim, and releases on disconnect. One place to change when the
contract evolves; a component that must not claim (Button, Panel)
simply never instantiates it.
declarations.name: FieldClaimController

declarations.description:
Base class for every custom element in this package — enforces
GUIDELINES.md rule 3: a shadow root renders nothing but `<slot>`.
Subclasses add reactive properties and behavior, never markup.

Also owns the element's one `ElementInternals` handle (`attachInternals()`
throws if called twice, so it has to live in exactly one place) and a
`toggleState()` helper, because `CustomStateSet` ships `add`/`delete` but
no `toggleAttribute`-style toggle. Custom states are how a component
exposes *derived* state to its own `:host(:state(...))` CSS — state the
consumer sets stays a reflected attribute instead. See GUIDELINES.md
rule 4.
declarations.name: SlottedElement

declarations.description:
A pure slot — the projected content owns the actual dot's shape; this
element only owns filling/centering itself in its parent box and mapping
its own state to design tokens (GUIDELINES.md rule 3), both of which are
tag-name-agnostic via :host and so survive a consumer renaming the tag.

Consumes hwc-radio's state over context and mirrors it into custom
states on its own ElementInternals — never as attributes, so the light
DOM stays entirely the consumer's (GUIDELINES.md rule 4). Because the
visibility runs entirely on the radio's own state, a lone
`<hwc-radio checked>` — no group, no form, no name — always renders its
dot correctly. Not self-registering — call
RadioCheckedIndicator.define() (optionally with a tag name of your own
choosing) before use. See GUIDELINES.md rule 5.
declarations.name: RadioCheckedIndicator

slots.description: The consumer's own selection dot (an SVG, a glyph, anything).

declarations.name: radioContext
declarations.description:
Broadcasts hwc-radio's state to its checked-indicator child so it can
decide its own visibility — the same root-to-indicator pattern as
checkbox-context.ts. Nothing here identifies a descendant by tag name —
see GUIDELINES.md rules 4 and 5 for why that matters once tag names are
consumer-configurable.

declarations.name: radioGroupContext
declarations.description:
Provided by hwc-radio-group to descendant radios: the shared (or
auto-generated) name and a group-wide disabled. Context rather than
direct parentage because a radio is commonly wrapped in a hwc-field for
its label — the field sits between group and radio without knowing
either exists (GUIDELINES.md rule 4). A radio's own explicit `name`
attribute always wins over the context-provided one: the consumer's
attribute is the input API.

An optional convenience container for radios — not the grouping
mechanism itself. The registry (radio-registry.ts) owns mutual
exclusion, roving tabindex, and arrow keys; this element's job is to
hand descendants a shared name (auto-generated when absent) and a
group-wide disabled over context, plus carry role="radiogroup". Context
rather than direct parentage because a radio is commonly wrapped in a
hwc-field for its label (GUIDELINES.md rule 4).

Not self-registering — call RadioGroup.define() (optionally with a tag
name of your own choosing) before use. See GUIDELINES.md rule 5.
declarations.name: RadioGroup

slots.description: The group's radios, at any depth — commonly each wrapped in a field.

declarations.name: joinSet
declarations.description:
Adds `member` to the set for (scope, name), leaving any previous set
first. An empty name means "unnamed" — the member belongs to no set.
Re-joining the same key is a no-op.

declarations.name: leaveSet
declarations.description:
Removes `member` from its set, returning the remaining members in DOM
order so the caller can hand the departed member's tab stop to someone
else. No-op (empty array) if the member wasn't in a set.

declarations.name: setMembers
declarations.description: The member's whole set in DOM order; empty if it's unnamed (no set).

declarations.name: applyExclusion
declarations.description: Mutual exclusion: checking `member` unchecks every other member of its set.

declarations.name: syncTabStops
declarations.description:
Roving tabindex: exactly one member per set is in the tab order — the
checked one, or the first non-disabled in DOM order when none is checked
— so Tab crosses the whole set in one stop.

declarations.name: step
declarations.description:
The nearest non-disabled member `delta` steps away in DOM order,
wrapping at the ends; null when the member is alone, unnamed, or every
other member is disabled.

Headless radio root — state, behavior, and accessibility only.
See radio-button/SPEC.md for the composition contract and GUIDELINES.md
for why there's no native `<input type="radio">` underneath.

Grouping runs through the name registry (radio-registry.ts), scoped by
(internals.form ?? root node, name) exactly like native radios. A name
arrives from the consumer's attribute, or from a surrounding
hwc-radio-group over context — the attribute always wins. With no name
at all the radio is controlled: activation fires `change` without
mutating state, and the consumer commits `checked` themselves.

Form-associated (GUIDELINES.md rule 8): the checked member of a named
set submits `value` under the shared name, honors form.reset() and
`<fieldset disabled>`, and restores state on session restore. Outside a
form every one of those is a silent no-op.

Not self-registering — call Radio.define() (optionally with a tag name
of your own choosing) before use. See GUIDELINES.md rule 5.
declarations.name: Radio

events.name: change
events.description: Dispatched on user activation (click, Space, arrow-key movement). Named mode: state already changed — `target.checked` is the new value. Unnamed (controlled) mode: a request — nothing mutated, the consumer commits `checked` themselves. An already-checked radio fires nothing in either mode.

declarations.description:
A pure positional seam (root README's "positional seams" category) —
present only when the consumer projects one, giving a theme a fixed,
addressable box to size and center regardless of what's projected.
Carries no state and consumes none; disabled dimming reaches a
`currentColor`-based icon for free through ordinary CSS inheritance
from hwc-text-input's own `color`.

One wrinkle Button's icons don't have: this box sits *inside* an
editable host (SPEC.md § Editing model), so it marks itself
`contenteditable="false"` — a non-editable atomic island the root's
edit guard recognizes by that attribute, never by tag name.

Not self-registering — call TextInputLeadingIcon.define() (optionally
with a tag name of your own choosing) before use. See GUIDELINES.md
rule 5.
declarations.name: TextInputLeadingIcon

slots.description: The consumer's own icon (an SVG, an ``, anything).

declarations.description:
A pure positional seam like the leading icon — see
text-input-leading-icon.ts; the same editable-host wrinkle applies, so
this box also marks itself `contenteditable="false"`. When what's
projected is itself interactive (a clear button, a reveal toggle), that
inner control needs its own accessible name and must not steal focus
from the input on click (SPEC.md § Composition) — both the consumer's
responsibility, since the projected content is theirs.

Not self-registering — call TextInputTrailingIcon.define() (optionally
with a tag name of your own choosing) before use. See GUIDELINES.md
rule 5.
declarations.name: TextInputTrailingIcon

slots.description: The consumer's own icon or trailing control.

declarations.description:
Headless single-line text input root — state, behavior, and accessibility
only. See text-input/SPEC.md for the composition contract and
GUIDELINES.md rule 2 for why there's no native `<input>` underneath: the
host itself is the editable surface (contenteditable="plaintext-only"),
and the shadow root's `<slot>` projects the light-DOM text being edited,
so caret, selection, and IME composition are the platform's own.

The parts the platform *doesn't* give are rebuilt here (SPEC.md):
- Value model: the projected text is the value; the `value` attribute is
  the default, tracked under native's dirty-value-flag rules and never
  reflected back.
- Edit guard: beforeinput operations whose target range touches a
  non-text child (an icon part — a contenteditable="false" island), or
  that would insert newlines, are cancelled and re-performed against the
  text only. Ordinary typing is never intercepted. The guard is dormant
  during IME composition.
- Form contract (GUIDELINES.md rule 8): live setFormValue on every edit,
  Enter-to-submit (the reimplemented implicit submission), reset to the
  markup default, session restore, fieldset disable.
- Selection API parity: select(), setSelectionRange(), and
  selectionStart/selectionEnd/selectionDirection, matching
  HTMLInputElement's own — cached rather than read live from the
  platform selection so they persist across blur the same way native's
  does (see the field declarations' own comment).

Not self-registering — call TextInput.define() (optionally with a tag
name of your own choosing) before use. See GUIDELINES.md rule 5.
declarations.name: TextInput

slots.description: The text being edited, plus optional leading/trailing icon parts.

members.name: value
members.description:
The current value — the projected light-DOM text itself (direct child
text nodes; icon subtrees excluded). Never reflected to the `value`
attribute, which stays the markup-declared default (SPEC § Value model).

members.name: select
members.description:
Selects all the text — matches native <input>.select(), including its
documented side effect of focusing the element if it wasn't already.

members.name: setSelectionRange
members.description:
Sets the selection to [start, end), matching HTMLInputElement's own
algorithm: end is clamped to the value's length first, then start is
clamped to at most that (a start past end collapses to end, it is
never swapped with it) — direction defaults to "none" and any other
value also normalizes to "none", same as native. Also focuses the
element: unlike a native input, which tracks selection independently
of focus, this component's selection *is* the document Selection API
(SPEC § Editing model), so setting it while unfocused would otherwise
silently steal whatever selection is active elsewhere on the page.

members.name: selectionStart
members.description:
The offset of the selection's start — persists across blur (tabbing
back in restores it), same as native, since it's cached rather than
read fresh from the platform selection every time (see the field's
own comment for why).

members.name: selectionEnd
members.description: The offset of the selection's end.

events.name: change
events.description: Dispatched after the value changed, on commit: blur, or Enter before submission.
